_comment: Hand-written correctness cases (the only hand-written fixtures). Each carries `expect_output`; the fixture declares `function main()` and the runner `cargo run`s it, comparing stdout. `console.log(x)` lowers to `println!("{}", x)` (Display, not Debug), so fixtures log primitives or joined strings — never a bare Vec/struct.

features.fixture:
function main(): void { const xs: number[] = [1, 2, 3]; console.log(xs.join("-")); }
main();

features.note: JSON.stringify(42) inlines serde_json::to_string (serde_json dep injected, no __ds helper); prints 42

features.fixture:
function main(): void { let m: Map<string, number> = new Map(); m.set("a", 1); console.log(m.size); console.log(m.has("a")); console.log(m.has("b")); }
main();
features.note: Map<K,V> -> HashMap; set/size/has map to insert/len/contains_key

features.fixture:
function main(): void { let s: Set<string> = new Set(); s.add("a"); s.add("b"); s.add("a"); console.log(s.size); console.log(s.has("b")); }
main();
features.note: Set<T> -> HashSet<T: Hash+Eq>; string elements work (number can't — f64 has no Eq)

features.fixture:
function main(): void { console.log(atob(btoa("hello"))); console.log(btoa("A")); }
main();
features.note: WinterTC base64: btoa('hello')='aGVsbG8=' then atob -> 'hello'; btoa('A')='QQ=='

features.fixture:
function main(): void { const s: string = "abc"; console.log(structuredClone(s)); }
main();
features.note: structuredClone(v) -> v.clone() (DashScript values are Clone); a primitive clone is itself

features.fixture:
function main(): void { const t: number = performance.now(); console.log(t > 0); }
main();
features.note: WinterTC hr-time: performance.now() returns a monotonic ms value > 0

features.fixture:
function main(): void { const a: number = self.performance.now(); const b: number = self.performance.now(); console.log(b - a >= 0); }
main();
features.note: WinterTC self global alias: self.performance.now() lowers the same as performance.now(); monotonic difference is non-negative
